title: The Ambo: The Pulpit of Light
english: Now I must also describe the Ambo, that marvel of workmanship which stands in the midst of the church, where the sacred readings are proclaimed. It is approached by winding stairs on either side, and its form is octagonal, rising in graceful stages to a height befitting the proclamation of the divine word.

Its columns are of precious marble, green as the sea, and its capitals are carved with the vine and the cross. Upon its parapets are silver discs, chased with the figures of the prophets and the apostles, each bearing his symbol. In the center, above the place where the deacon stands, the cross blazes in gold and gems, the sign of our salvation.

From the Ambo the deacon cries aloud the Gospel, and his voice is carried on the air to every corner of the great church, as though the dome itself were a great ear listening to the word of God. The light from the lamps above falls upon the reader, making a crown of light about his head.

title: Conclusion: The Church as Cosmic Liturgy
english: Thus the church of the Holy Wisdom stands complete, a wonder of the age, a crown of the city, a harbor of light for those who sail the stormy seas of this life. Its dome is the firmament, its lamps the stars, its cross the guardian, its Ambo the mount of proclamation.

Here the emperor, the new Constantine, offers his crown to the King of kings; here the patriarch, the new Aaron, offers the unbloody sacrifice; here the people, the new Israel, offer the sacrifice of praise. The sacred light cheers all: even the sailor guiding his bark on the waves, leaving behind him the unfriendly billows of the raging Pontus, and winding a sinuous course amidst creeks and rocks, with heart fearful at the dangers of his nightly wanderings — does not guide his laden vessel by the light of Cynosure, or the circling Bear, but by the divine light of the church itself. Yet not only does it guide the merchant at night, like the rays from the Pharos on the coast of Africa, but it also shows the way to the living God.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
